paragraphs.text: A healthy, attractive smile means confidence inside and out. Current Orthodontics offers the most current, state-of-the-art orthodontic treatments, from the virtually invisible Invisalign system to low-profile, lightweight metal braces.

paragraphs.text: Dr. Jon Petersen strongly feels that orthodontics is about more than just straightening teeth. It is about building confidence, self-esteem, oral health, and enabling people to get the most out of their lives. His primary focus is creating a patient-focused practice, providing the highest level of clinical excellence in a timely, efficient manner while offering options that fit each patient’s needs, desires, and budget.

We offer free consultations so each person can learn about their options and decide on a treatment plan that fits their lifestyle and goals. We take time to explain choices and make sure families feel comfortable with every step of care.

Our treatment options include metal and ceramic braces, Invisalign<sup>®</sup> for eligible cases, and advanced care when patients need orthognathic collaboration, TMJ support, or temporary anchorage devices. We combine modern technology with thoughtful techniques to achieve healthy, attractive results.

Comfort, clear communication, and flexible scheduling are central to how we work. From weekend appointment availability to helpful financial coordination, our team supports patients and families through every visit and beyond.

image.alt: Dr. Jon Petersen headshot

paragraphs.text: Dr. Jon Petersen strongly feels that orthodontics is about more than just straightening teeth. It is about building confidence, self-esteem, oral health, and enabling people to get the most out of their lives. His primary focus is creating a patient focused practice, and takes great pride in providing the highest of clinical excellence in a timely, efficient manner.
He understands that each patient has different needs, desires, and budgets, and he welcomes free consultations to review individual options and answer questions so families can make informed choices.

image.alt: Dr. Jon Petersen smiling in the office

paragraphs.text: Dr. Petersen studied Medical Biology at the University of Utah and earned his Doctor of Medicine in Dentistry from the Medical University of South Carolina, graduating at the top of his class and receiving honors including Orthodontic Student of the Year and induction into Omicron Kappa Upsilon.

He completed orthodontic specialty training at Montefiore Medical Center, gaining advanced experience in smile esthetics, orthognathic surgery collaboration, Invisalign therapy, laser gingival contouring, TMJ treatment, and temporary anchorage device placement. Dr. Petersen is a member of the Umpqua Dental Society and the American Dental Association, and is board‑eligible with the American Orthodontic Organization.

image.alt: Dr. Jon Petersen headshot

paragraphs.text: Dr. Petersen has published research on esthetic orthodontic options and TMJ pain and treatment, and he regularly presents at conferences and engages with ongoing orthodontic research to stay current with best practices.
He lives in Roseburg with his wife Katherine and son Jack, and he enjoys snowboarding in winter and hiking, biking, and fishing in Oregon’s outdoors during the summer.

paragraphs.text: Although metal braces are often called “traditional braces,” today’s brackets are lighter and more comfortable. They’re an effective, economical option for a wide range of cases. For patients seeking an invisible look, braces can be placed on the backs of teeth (lingual braces).

image.alt: Dental Checkup with Braces

paragraphs.text: Ceramic braces are designed to blend with your tooth color, offering a less noticeable option without sacrificing effectiveness. They work similarly to metal braces but are often chosen for their subtle appearance.

image.alt: Smiling Woman with Clear Aligner

paragraphs.text: Damon braces use a sliding mechanism built into each bracket instead of ligatures. That self‑ligating design typically means smaller brackets, easier cleaning, fewer adjustments, and greater comfort for many patients.

image.alt: Two stylish smiling teens taking selfie with braces

paragraphs.text: Lingual braces are attached to the back surfaces of teeth, making them virtually invisible from the front. They offer an effective option for patients who want powerful tooth movement without visible brackets.

image.alt: Smiling family enjoying time together

paragraphs.text: Invisalign<sup>®</sup> uses a series of clear, removable aligners to gently move teeth. The aligners are made from advanced 3D-planned designs that fit precisely and let you brush, floss, and eat without bracket restrictions.
In many cases Invisalign<sup>®</sup> is suitable for teens and adults and can address gaps, crowding, and bite concerns with a discreet, convenient approach.

image.alt: Close-up of Invisalign aligners being placed on teeth

paragraphs.text: Propel is an accelerated-orthodontics option that can reduce treatment time by stimulating natural bone remodeling. It’s compatible with both braces and clear aligners and typically involves short in‑office sessions to support faster movement.

image.alt: 3D treatment planning software showing orthodontic simulation

paragraphs.text: We offer in‑office Opalescence whitening for noticeable results in under an hour. This professional system delivers brighter results than typical take‑home kits and is often combined with orthodontic care when appropriate.

image.alt: Modern dentist office interior with advanced technology

paragraphs.text: If a bracket comes loose, a wire breaks, or you’re experiencing prolonged soreness, there are simple steps you can take at home before contacting us. Protect your mouth with orthodontic wax, use gentle pain relief, and call the office to schedule a repair appointment when needed.
Remove a completely detached bracket from the mouth to avoid swallowing it. If the bracket is still on the wire, apply wax to prevent irritation and call us to arrange a reattachment.

image.alt: Braces in Roseburg with Current Orthodontics

paragraphs.text: Protect your mouth from any poking wire by applying orthodontic wax. If you must trim a protruding wire, clean and sterilize a nail clipper first. Call our office to arrange a replacement appointment.

image.alt: Dental Checkup with Braces

paragraphs.text: Soreness after an adjustment is common for a few days. Over‑the‑counter pain relievers, soft foods, cold treats, and warm salt‑water rinses can help. Call us if soreness persists beyond a few days.

paragraphs.text: Download and complete your new patient paperwork before your visit. Email completed forms to treatmentcoordinator@currentorthodontics.com or print and bring them to your appointment. paragraphs.text: After new braces or an adjustment you may feel soreness for a few days. Over‑the‑counter pain relievers like ibuprofen or acetaminophen can help, and cold foods offer temporary relief. If soreness persists beyond a few days or you have an emergency, call our office for guidance.

image.alt: Close-up of braces and orthodontic hardware in a treatment room

paragraphs.text: To protect patients and staff we ask that anyone with fever, cough, recent travel, or exposure to large gatherings reschedule. Our team wears masks, shields, goggles, and gowns. We limit waiting room guests when possible and have removed communal items like magazines. Virtual visits are available for new and existing patients. Sincerely, Dr. Petersen and Team.

image.alt: Orthodontic team wearing masks and protective gear in a treatment room
